title: targetdir.bats's no-cargo arm hides only the first cargo on PATH, and by substring, so on a machine with a second cargo it still finds one and fails (K115 on kovacs)
body:
K115 ran the full suite on kovacs (Ubuntu ARM64) at main c4f52b8e on 2026-10-26. It failed this arm of tests/unit/targetdir.bats and nothing else: "a machine config with no crate here and cargo not on PATH is reported as not measured, saying so once (0164)". The failure is at its first assertion (line 773), `assert_output_contains "cargo is not on PATH, so where the machine's cargo config sends a build cannot be measured"`. devbin measured the machine config's fork instead: "machine .../fakecargo13/config.toml moves the build tree to /tmp/mw-nocargo, and no crate here builds with it". The seal is ~/work/devbin-vc/devbin-k115/tmp/test/20261026-0852.bats.out on kovacs.

## Cause

The arm hides cargo by shadowing one directory. It sets `d="$(dirname "$(command -v cargo)")"`, makes a directory $nc of links to everything in $d but cargo, and runs under `PATH="$nc:${PATH//"$d"/$nc}"`. That has two faults:

1. Only the first cargo on PATH is hidden. kovacs has two: Homebrew's in /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin, first, and rustup's in ~/.cargo/bin, after it. With the first hidden, rustup's was still found, and devbin gave the right answer for a PATH that holds a cargo. CI's Ubuntu runner and rhadamanth each have one cargo on PATH, which is why the arm passes there.
2. `${PATH//"$d"/$nc}` replaces $d wherever it occurs as a substring, so an entry that merely contains it is rewritten too, eg `${d}utils`. Were cargo ever in /bin, every entry ending in /bin would be.

No other arm hides a tool this way. Nothing else in tests/ takes `dirname "$(command -v ...)"` or edits PATH by substitution; the other tool-absent arms build a narrow PATH (fullcycle.bats's cargo and jq arms, surfaces.bats's rlwrap arm).

## Fix

The arm rebuilds PATH entry by entry. Each entry holding an executable cargo is replaced, in place, by its own shadow directory of links to everything in it but cargo, and every other entry stays as it is, in order. The arm fails by name when cargo is still found on that PATH, as fullcycle.bats's jq arm does, so a red names its cause. Test-only: no shipped file changes.

## Done when

1. On rhadamanth, with a second directory holding a link to the real cargo placed on PATH after the first, the arm fails on main as it did on kovacs, and passes at the fix.
2. targetdir.bats passes at the fix under BSD and GNU.
3. CI's run on the pushed head is green on Test on Ubuntu.

## Resolution

Fixed at bc9d80c0, which changes tests/unit/targetdir.bats alone, so no shipped file changes. cc built it in a scratch clone (4fcc4601 on 860436b0, 0233's fix), and vc landed it. The no-cargo arm now rebuilds PATH entry by entry: each entry holding an executable cargo is swapped, in place, for its own directory of links to everything in it but cargo, and every other entry stays as it is, in order. So no cargo is left on PATH however many the machine carries, and no entry is rewritten as text. The arm fails by name, "cargo is still on PATH", when a cargo is still found on that PATH, checked in a subshell.

- **Done when 1.** On rhadamanth, targetdir.bats alone under BSD, with a second directory on PATH, after /opt/homebrew/bin, holding a link to the real cargo. On main (a1ca020c), the no-cargo arm failed at its first assertion (line 773) as it did on kovacs, devbin measuring the machine config's fork instead, and no other arm failed. At the fix, with the same PATH, every arm passed.
- **Done when 2.** targetdir.bats alone at the fix, under BSD (with the second cargo, above) and under GNU (with a plain PATH): each TAP ran to its plan, and nothing failed or skipped. These runs and main's went one at a time under molt-vc's standing GO for light runs, relayed by vc, and the driver ended at 2026-10-26 09:35Z with rc 0. Critic leg: `intent critic shell --files tests/unit/targetdir.bats` from the clone's root, rc 0; it asked no rule of the file, so it says nothing about it.
- **Done when 3.** CI run 40349359447 on a81f0f98: green on Test on Ubuntu.
